pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/110387

Having this in now affords us not having to introduce version checks in the ES exporter later. We can simply use the same serialization logic for metric attributes as we do for other signals.
This also enables us to properly map `*.ip` fields to the ip field type as ip fields containing a list of IPs are not converted to a comma-separated list.
pr_comment: Hi @felixbarny, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

I'm still on the fence for adding IP fields to the tsid, it does seem wasteful.. I see that they're part of the ECS template, but this will likely penalize indexing performance. Do we believe there's value in doing so? @martijnvg fyi.

> I'm still on the fence for adding IP fields to the tsid, it does seem wasteful.. I see that they're part of the ECS template, but this will likely penalize indexing performance. Do we believe there's value in doing so? @martijnvg fyi.

What's the alternative here? Are you suggesting we should store IPs as keywords and use that as a dimension?

Or not use IPs as dimensions at all? I don't think that's a generic rule we can make. For example, if you want to track netflow metrics, your identifying dimensions are src/dest ip/port.

review_comment: In the multi valued case, do you often expect 4 ip values?
This is assuming that when there are multiple values, we'll likely have less than 10 (the default size for ArrayLists), but probably more than 2.

Do I understand correctly that array values will have the same name? If so, how do we guarantee that they won't be shuffled by sorting - default sorting is not stable?  

One option is to add a suffix to the name for array elements, e.g. `.0`, `.1` etc. This way, you don't need to touch this function?
Good catch. Adding the offset should be safe in terms of not changing existing _tsids because so far, we haven't allowed sources with an array value.
I solved a bit differently. But the ordering should be guaranteed now.

Do I understand correctly that the hash here depends on the order the fields get hashed? I wonder if we have issues if the fields get shuffled, i.e. `"foo": { "a": [1,2,3], "b": 10  }` and `"foo": { "b": 10, "a": [1,2,3] }` need to give the same hash.

No, the hashes get sorted by the field name, so the hash is consistent, regardless of the ordering of fields in the source. Where ordering matters is within arrays. This is why in the `compare to` method in `NameAndHash`, we're primarily sorting by the name, and the order is just the tie breaker, which only affects arrays, as that's the only way you can have two `NameAndHash` instances with the same name. This is also tested in `org.elasticsearch.cluster.routing.IndexRoutingTests#testRoutingPathArraysInSource`.
Nit: add a short comment that this wasn't supported in legacy tsid calculations.
